_why: The window each clip is read at in the runner's nightly (the EP's decision of 2026-11-14: a runner cannot read a whole clip, so each clip is read as a window at its worst moment, collapse at 60 ticks; the full reading stays a local run on Orb's PC). skip is run-pixels.mjs's --skip (ticks run without a picture first; the window starts at tick skip + 1). A clip with no entry is read from tick 1 for defaultTicks, the speed trial's way. 'from' says how the moment was found: an entry that has not been measured says so. tools/flash/nightly-windows.mjs --check reads this file. capMin is the clip's time cap in minutes (default defaultCapMin): the ticks skipped before a window cost time too, about 2.2 s a tick on a runner (run 43580079641: a skip of 950 plus 76 captured ticks used the 45 minutes), so a window far into a clip needs a longer cap than its captured ticks do. The analyser counts no change in the first 60 frames of a clip (its warm-up) and the two-second memory reading in the first 120, so a window needs more than 61 ticks, and about 120 ticks of lead-in before the moment it is meant to catch.

collapse-normal.from: Measured 2026-11-14 (hardware, 960x540, f1f91f45): full clip PASS at primary 2, worst second events at ticks 1111, 1132, 1145, 1151; the window (180 ticks from 991, with the 120 ticks of lead the memory reading needs) read the same ticks, the same primary 2 and memory 2. Not measured on a runner: collapse costs 20 to 50 s a tick there plus about 2 s a skipped tick, so the cap is 210 minutes.

collapse-reduced.from: Measured 2026-11-14 (hardware, 960x540, f1f91f45): full clip OVER our gate at primary 3 (memory 2.5), worst second events at ticks 1465 to 1499, the end of the clip (the worst moment may run on past tick 1500); the window (160 ticks from 1341) read the same ticks, primary 3 and memory 2.5. A window of 130 from 1371 read the same primary but a memory of 1: the memory reading ignores its first 120 frames. Not measured on a runner (cap 210 minutes).

clash-normal.from: ticks 951 to 1120 (170): the full local reading of clash-normal (960x540, hardware, 2026-11-14, HEAD 97df40b8 export) has its worst second at ticks 1075 to 1113 and a two-second memory of 4; this window read the same ticks (one a tick off), the same primary 4.5 and a memory of 4.5. A window from tick 1011 (125 ticks) read the same worst second but a memory of 0.5, because the memory reading ignores its first 120 frames: so the window starts at 951. Cost on a runner: about 35 minutes of skipped ticks plus about 23 of captured ones. Run 43585295274 (software rendering on a runner, cap 90 min) read this window in 5173 s (86 min): primary 4.5, two-second memory 4.5, the same as the hardware full reading; the cap is now 150 because three other clash windows of the same run timed out at 90.

signature-normal.from: Measured 2026-11-14 (hardware, 960x540, export of f1f91f45): the full clip reads its worst second at ticks 76 to 129 (events 76, 82, 110, 114, 125, 127, 129), so the window starts at tick 1 and runs 180 ticks. The reading is on the line of 3 and moves by half a flash to one flash from run to run: the full clip read 3.5 and then 3, the window read 3, 2.5 and 2.5 (the reduced window matched its full reading exactly). Treat a signature window as a tripwire within one flash of the line, not as the clip's number.
